quotes.text: your Dashboard settings can’t add payment methods that the code doesn’t allow.
the connected account’s payment method settings determine which payment methods are available.
A payment method that isn’t in `allowed_payment_method_types` can’t appear, even if you turn it on in the Dashboard.
Starting with API version `2026-09-30.endive`, you can’t pass `payment_method_types` when you create Checkout Sessions, PaymentIntents, or SetupIntents.
The order of `allowed_payment_method_types` doesn’t determine the display order:

old_evidence.text: Every payment method you want your PaymentIntent to accept must be added to `payment_method_types`.
If multiple payment methods are passed, Checkout dynamically reorders them to prioritize the most relevant payment methods based on the customer’s location and other characteristics.

findings: November explicitly separates dynamic Dashboard management, code restriction, transaction compatibility and UI order at new 9–39. An authorized Dashboard role is needed, some methods require activation, approval or invite, and some wallets such as Apple Pay require registering the domain for Elements or embedded Checkout. Connected-account settings govern direct or on_behalf_of charges. The merchant or authorized account user can toggle dynamic methods without code changes, and Stripe may enable additional defaults after notice. The Dashboard cannot add a type excluded by code. Old 8–15,23–37,39–49 and source 27,33 retain earlier compatibility/recommendation but omit the specific permission, activation, some-method registration modality and Connect distinction.

New 43–83 uses allowed_payment_method_types as the Checkout Session or PaymentIntent create request allowlist. Stripe filters to compatible methods by transaction amount, currency and customer; payment_method_types is the output subset. Out-of-list methods cannot appear even when Dashboard-enabled, and allowlist order does not set display order (new 47,85–88). Older 51–87 and source 35 used payment_method_types as request with equivalent example entries. Starting 2026-09-30.endive, the old field cannot be passed when creating Checkout Sessions, PaymentIntents or SetupIntents. Earlier GA Checkout uses old request field as stated by current guide; PaymentIntents and SetupIntents accept allowed_payment_method_types from 2026-07-29.dahlia. Preserve old code examples as versioned, not as current defaults.

Scoped changelog evidence verifies automatic incompatible-type filtering rather than earlier explicit-list errors. July 29 Dahlia for PaymentIntents/SetupIntents, September 30 Endive for Checkout Session new filter and removed field. The July Intent release explicitly makes the allowlist mutually exclusive with legacy request list, exclusion list, automatic_payment_methods and payment_method_configuration (extra Dahlia 9–21). The Endive Checkout release says old create field gives 400 (extra Checkout Endive 9–23); Intent release extends writable removal to PaymentIntent update/confirm and SetupIntent update, and the 400 code payment_method_types_no_longer_supported is stated for those Intent endpoints (extra Intent Endive 9–22). Do not generalize all affected endpoints or the code across resources. No version is inferred from a code snippet alone.

New 35–41 adds per-transaction excluded_payment_method_types for Dashboard-managed dynamic methods, a separate approach from allowlist, and explicitly distinguishes eligible-set filtering from Checkout dynamic order and the Payment Element default/order override paymentMethodOrder (new 28–41,85–88). Scoped November dynamic guide lines 89–105 shows exclusions across named surfaces and the integration-specific wallets hash for Apple Pay, Google Pay and Link instead of that exclusion field for a PaymentIntent. May 89 describes Checkout reorders and moves low priority to overflow. November retains ordering, omits overflow and does not show individual ranking, revocation or ordering of unsupported methods.

Both table views preserve the five website paths, underlying APIs, hosting/coding, limited customization versus Appearance API and wallet routes. November labels/formatting and replaces Node with cURL examples; it adds explicit BNPL support across the five paths subject to method eligibility, Dashboard support footnote conditional on dynamic integration, and 'eligible payment methods' in place of '40+' without a changed count assertion. Custom payment methods moves from advanced-only May comparison row to support varies with a dedicated integration route (old 16–33; new 90–116). Scoped May 8, 2026 custom-method matrix 68–76 already includes other product contexts such as mobile/payment element and Billing routes; the November custom-method matrix 57–75 adds Checkout support and Express Checkout Element private preview but still excludes Payment Links. Interpret exact version and product route rather than importing universal support. Source 25 and concept 82 must date the old five-path assertion.

Both retain Stripe Invoicing saved-method auto charge or email without code where supported (old 14 and new 94). Quickstart, default payment methods, other integrations and pricing links are routes, not proof of specific account eligibility, default revocation, payment acceptance or runtime behavior. Preserve older comparison labels, 40+ and overflow as May guide statements.

source_assessments.reason: November materially changes the versioned request field, adds eligibility/default/code and actor boundaries, and revises the custom/BNPL and registration descriptions. Preserve dated original examples but refresh primary retrieval.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/integration-options, November documents how authorized Dashboard users enable eligible methods in a dynamic integration, while integration code can further restrict the eligible set; Dashboard cannot add a method outside code. Account authorization/invite and domain registration for some wallets are prerequisites, and Connected Account settings apply to direct or on_behalf_of charges. Stripe filters by compatibility, and only then does Checkout or Payment Element order remaining methods (old raw lines 8-49 and new raw lines 9-41). The merchant’s Checkout Session/PaymentIntent create allowlist filters silently to compatible types seen in the response payment_method_types. Endive 2026-09-30 removes that name as a writable create parameter across Checkout Sessions, PaymentIntents and SetupIntents. Dahlia 2026-07-29 already offers the allowlist for PaymentIntents/SetupIntents, whereas earlier GA Checkout uses the old request parameter. Dashboard dynamic exclusion is separate, and Payment Element has a presentation order override (old raw lines 51-89 and new raw lines 43-88). source-stripe-payment-method-integration-options.md captures May's five UI/API options and its manual list, but needs dates, the source’s new version gates, eligibility versus order, and corrected wallet and custom-method scope. Configuration/compatible response is distinct from payment execution.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/integration-options, November materially adds the earlier-GA, July Dahlia and September Endive request boundaries, compatible response subset, explicit Dashboard/code/eligibility/order distinctions, role/approval/domain prerequisites, Connect ownership and per-transaction exclusions. It qualifies Dashboard changes as dynamic-only, adds a BNPL row and replaces the prior advanced-only custom-method label with a scope-dependent route (old raw lines 16-37 and 43-89, new raw lines 9-88 and 90-116). Preserve May 1's five paths, older request examples, numeric 40+ marketing and priority overflow as dated language. Node-to-cURL presentation, table renames, pricing/quickstart links and reordering are presentational or navigation, while updated request parameters are substantive. Preserve the external versioned incompatibility behavior and custom-method product boundaries already verified, without promising specific eligibility. Update source-stripe-payment-method-integration-options.md and retain May raw provenance, the root-to-Stripe index and reciprocal Stripe Payment Methods concept/source route, with separate Dynamic Payment Methods, domain registration and support references.
